title: Unified Static-Dynamic Pruning for Efficient LLM Inference
event_hint: SPDP: a unified sparse-inference framework integrating unstructured static weight pruning with input-adaptive dynamic pruning via a Tiled-CBC format and dual GPU kernels (spMspV decode + Tensor-Core SpMM prefill), published at PVLDB 19(11) 2026.
problem: Autoregressive LLM decoding is dominated by memory-bandwidth-bound, low-compute-intensity kernels. Static pruning (SP) permanently removes weights but lacks adaptivity; dynamic pruning (DP) adapts to input sparsity but introduces runtime irregularity. Existing systems (Flash-LLM, SpInfer) rely only on static sparsity, forfeiting input-adaptive redundancy. The two paradigms were not directly composable: SP kernels are row-major SpMM-optimized while DP induces column-wise spMspV workloads, disrupting coalesced access and Tensor Core utilization.
mechanism: SPDP co-designs the Tiled-Column-wise Bitmap Compressed (Tiled-CBC) format that encodes statically pruned weights in column-major micro-tiles aligned with DP activation sparsity. Two kernels: (1) a CUDA-core spMspV kernel with Hybrid Activation-aware Dynamic Shared-Memory Bitmap Decoding (HAD-SMBD) for fine-grained runtime activation skipping during decode; (2) a Tensor-Core SpMM kernel for prefill using the same format via shared-memory layout alignment. SP and DP act on orthogonal dimensions (SP prunes weights across rows, DP skips activations across columns), so their sparsity patterns multiply effective sparsity.

evidence.claim: SPDP achieves 1.24x-1.37x average kernel speedup (up to 2.51x) over state-of-the-art sparse frameworks such as SpInfer on inference-optimized GPUs, while matching perplexity with up to 25% higher sparsity.
evidence.value: 1.24x-1.37x avg (up to 2.51x); +25% sparsity at matched perplexity
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 1 - Abstract; PDF Page 10 - Figure 8

evidence.claim: Kernel-level (A10G): SPDP-spMspV averages 1.88x over cuBLAS and 1.24x over SpInfer (max 3.32x / 1.70x); on L4, averages 2.11x over cuBLAS and 1.37x over SpInfer (max 3.52x / 2.52x).

End-to-end (LLaMA-2-7B): SPDP achieves average 1.34x TPOT speedup over SpInfer at comparable moderate sparsity while maintaining lower perplexity (under 5.4); perplexity diverges sharply beyond 70% static sparsity.

Hardware profiling (A10G, (DP,SP)=(30%,30%)): SPDP-spMspV attains the highest SM busy (66.0%) vs SpInfer 30% (48.0%) and SpInfer 50% (38.2%), lowest bank conflicts (74 vs 3817/449), with comparable Max bandwidth (87.3% vs 84.4-87.4%).

Evaluation uses LLM projection matrix shapes from OPT (13B-175B), LLaMA-2 (7B-70B), LLaMA-3 (8B,70B), Qwen (7B,14B), Qwen2 (7B,72B), Mixtral-8x7B MoE, Phi-2/3, gpt-oss (20B,120B); baselines: cuBLAS, cuSPARSE, Sputnik, SparTA, Flash-LLM, SpInfer.
evidence.baseline: cuBLAS, cuSPARSE, Sputnik, SparTA, Flash-LLM, SpInfer
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 10 - LLM projection matrix

evaluation_context: Kernel-level and end-to-end evaluation on inference-optimized GPUs: NVIDIA A10G, L4, L40S. Workloads: LLM projection matrix shapes from major architectures (OPT 13B-175B, LLaMA-2 7B-70B, LLaMA-3 8B/70B, Qwen 7B/14B, Qwen2 7B/72B, Mixtral-8x7B MoE, Phi-2/3, gpt-oss 20B/120B). Practical sparsity range 30-50% for both SP and DP. End-to-end model: LLaMA-2-7B-hf. Baselines: cuBLAS (dense), cuSPARSE, Sputnik, SparTA, Flash-LLM, SpInfer. Metrics: kernel TFLOP/s, TPOT, perplexity, SM busy, Max bandwidth, bank conflicts. Source code at github.com/AIDASLab/SPDP.
limitations: End-to-end gains are modest (Amdahl-style ceiling) because many decode components (attention, normalization) are not sparsity-sensitive and decoding is memory-bound. Quantization and unstructured sparsity do not provide multiplicative compression in practice (low-bit precision reduces only Values; bitmap/colinfo/tileoffset metadata remain). SPDP targets moderate-sparsity LLM decode; on extremely sparse matrices (e.g., SuiteSparse) existing works may be superior. No production deployment scale, power-in-watts, or serving-end-to-end (continuous batching) latency numbers are in the visible evidence; energy-efficiency claims are qualitative ('meaningfully decreases data movement').
project_relevance: SPDP is a GPU kernel/format co-design for sparse LLM inference, directly relevant to serving-runtime/compiler optimization and decode memory-bandwidth bottlenecks. It offers a concrete mechanism (unified static-dynamic pruning with Tiled-CBC) for improving decode throughput and performance-per-watt. For the project card it is a research system with kernel and end-to-end (LLaMA-2-7B) results on inference GPUs, not a production deployment.
